There were no storms in the data this week. The latest snapshot shows zero weather alerts in all eight tracked states. The six Punctual Pros hubs shown were dry, mild and breezy from Nov 7 to Nov 11, 2026, so weather-driven demand above the seasonal baseline is unlikely (est.).

What it means for demand

  • No storm trigger is visible. Plumbing and electrical demand should run near the seasonal baseline (est.).

  • Historical context. The storm events file covers significant NWS-reported events. It does not cover routine cool or windy days, so it cannot benchmark this week (Punctual Pros storm events).

Next actions

  1. Refresh the alert and forecast snapshots for all ten hubs. Confirm Nov 11–15 snow and wind.
  2. Pull Punctual Pros ServiceTitan booked calls by trade for Nov 7–12. Compare them with the same weeks in prior years to test whether the cold nights moved HVAC volume.
  3. Load the November monthly index, county households and a market-share estimate. This produces a dated expected-calls figure (est.).

# Punctual Pros: this week's storm exposure

There were no storms in the data this week. The latest snapshot shows zero weather alerts in all eight tracked states. The six Punctual Pros hubs shown were dry, mild and breezy from Nov 7 to Nov 11, 2026, so weather-driven demand above the seasonal baseline is unlikely (est.).

## What the data shows

- **Alerts:** zero NWS alerts in PA, NJ, MA, CT, RI, NH, ME and VT as of Nov 9, 2026 (National Weather Service alerts).
- **Precipitation:** 0.0 every day at every hub shown. Rain chance peaked at 15 (Open-Meteo 7-day forecast).
- **Snow:** 0.0 from Nov 7 to Nov 10. The Nov 11 snow value is cut off in the snapshot.
- **Temperatures:** highs ran 55.3–66.4 and lows bottomed at 37.2–39.1 (units as reported).
- **Wind:** gusts reached 35.3 at Carlisle on Nov 8. Gusts eased to 17.9–27.3 by Nov 11.

| Lebanon | 31.5 | 37.7 | 0.0 |

*Nov 7–11, 2026 (Open-Meteo 7-day forecast). Four of the ten hubs are not shown in the snapshot.*

## What it means for demand

- **No storm trigger is visible.** Plumbing and electrical demand should run near the seasonal baseline (est.).
- **Cold nights could matter for HVAC.** Lows near 37 may prompt some heating start-up calls. The heating multipliers are assumptions, not fitted values, so this is directional only (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Gusts in the low-to-mid 30s did not trigger alerts.** The model's wind thresholds are not in the context, so whether these gusts activate the electrical multiplier cannot be confirmed.

## What we cannot quantify

- **Expected call counts.** These need county household counts, the November monthly index by trade, and Punctual Pros market share. Market share is an unset parameter (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Nov 12 onward.** The snapshot was fetched Nov 9, 2026 and is truncated after Nov 11. It is three days old.
- **Historical context.** The storm events file covers significant NWS-reported events. It does not cover routine cool or windy days, so it cannot benchmark this week (Punctual Pros storm events).

## Next actions

1. Refresh the alert and forecast snapshots for all ten hubs. Confirm Nov 11–15 snow and wind.
2. Pull Punctual Pros ServiceTitan booked calls by trade for Nov 7–12. Compare them with the same weeks in prior years to test whether the cold nights moved HVAC volume.
3. Load the November monthly index, county households and a market-share estimate. This produces a dated expected-calls figure (est.).
4. Start the regression calibration once 12+ months of Punctual Pros call data are loaded. This would replace the assumed heating and wind multipliers.
